alignments.note: Existential negative with its supplied dummy and copula, headed on the negation word (rule 50).

`לְ` rendered *of*.

The appositional *even* stands before a phrase no object marker marks — the following phrase carries a `לְ`, not an `אֵת` — so no morpheme licenses it (rules 16, 30). The alternative reads it with the following `לְ`.
`לְ` rendered *of*.

Quantifier with the generic pronoun the ASV supplies to expand it into an antecedent for the relative; the supplied word joins the quantifier's unit and the head stays on the word carrying the lexeme (rules 31, 46).

The relative and the resumptive suffix of `לִפְנֵיהֶם` share the single word *whom*, which carries the relation and the resumption alike, so the suffix is not marked unrepresented (rule 22's resumptive-suffix paragraph, on rule 30's one-English-word condition); headed on the relative. The suffix is 3mp and denotes the antecedent `כֹל`, which is the referent test that rule makes decisive. The competing reading gives the suffix the *them* of *all them*, but that word stands outside the relative clause as its antecedent.

Substantival adjective rendered *come after*, headed on the word carrying the lexeme by rule 31's subtraction test.

review_notes: Corrected: the resumptive suffix of `לִפְנֵיהֶם` had been marked unrepresented beside a bare `אֲשֶׁר` → *whom*. Rule 22 forbids that where the one English word carries the resumption as well as the relation, so the relative and the suffix now share one unit on *whom*, headed on the relative, while `לִפְנֵי` keeps its own *over*, exactly as the noun keeps *stones* in that rule's `whose` case.
*all them* stays with `כֹל` as rule 31's supplied completion of the quantifier: *them* stands outside the relative clause as its antecedent, so it cannot be the clause-internal resumption.
The marginal note offering *There is no end, in the mind of all the people...* was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
